html:
A settlement founded in 1787 on the Sierra Leone peninsula by about 400 Black Londoners, the so-called Black Poor, with some white women, under a plan of Granville Sharp and other abolitionists.

Many had been freed for fighting for Britain in the American war. They named their town Granville Town and planned to govern themselves. Disease, bad timing with the rains and quarrels with traders killed many, and in 1789 a local Temne ruler burned the town after a dispute. Survivors joined the Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia who founded Freetown in 1792. The idea of a free Black settlement shaped both Sierra Leone and later Liberia.
